EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a single strong C=O stretching band at 1711 cm⁻¹, the normal position for a saturated, non-conjugated ketone. No amide (≈1650 cm⁻¹) or aromatic (≈1600 cm⁻¹, 3050 cm⁻¹) bands are present, excluding candidates that contain amide or aromatic groups. Intense aliphatic C–H stretches at 2870–2954 cm⁻¹ indicate only sp³ C-H bonds, matching a cycloalkyl ketone. Characteristic ring deformation/breathing bands for a six-membered alicyclic ketone appear at 754 cm⁻¹ and 843 cm⁻¹, and strong C–C stretching/CH₂ rocking bands are seen at 1020, 994 and 657 cm⁻¹, all features reported for cyclohexanone. Among the candidates, only “O=C1CCCCC1” (cyclohexanone) provides exactly one non-conjugated carbonyl in a six-membered aliphatic ring and no other functional groups, matching the observed pattern.
